name: m4-uniques-rejuv

variantDescriptions.weak: `claude/uniques-audit` `41986b33ea` (retronym/scala#212 + #239 + census probe, census off) with today's `WeakHashSet` table
variantDescriptions.rejuv: chunked-weak, and after each GC (a cleared `WeakReference` canary) every chunk written 256+ times since the previous GC is copied, so it is young again and inserts into it dirty no cards (from retronym/interner-gc-bench)
variantDescriptions.uncache-all: chunked-weak, and types made in the weak scopes are not interned (shared only if already in the table or a 4096-slot direct-mapped cache)

description: Does copying written chunks young after each GC (chunk rejuvenation) cut scalac's GC pauses? A debug GC log of one scala-corpus compile per variant (laptop, job 552) showed the chunked layout removes humongous regions (43 to 12) but cuts scanned cards only 9%, because the chunks tenure within a compile; not interning weak-scope types cut cards 57% and pauses 33%. A laptop pilot of rejuvenation (job 555, one fork each) was inconclusive: pauses rejuv -9%, rejuv-uncache -15% vs weak, scanned cards no lower, and 38-40 young GCs per fork instead of 34.
Separate forks (paired forks distort the mutator through a shared call site), same setup as `m4-uniques-uncache` (job 546). Read GC pause sums from `gc.log` as well as the score.
